newsitem.title: RUSSIA: 48 feared killed in Russian passenger plane crash.
newsitem.headline: 48 feared killed in Russian passenger plane crash.

text.p: A Russian AN-24 passenger plane crashed on Tuesday in the North Caucasus region and all 48 people on board were feared killed, a spokesman for the Emergencies Ministry said.
"We are not absolutely sure, but according to preliminary information, all of them have been killed," the Moscow-based spokesman said by telephone.
He said the plane, carrying seven crew and 41 passengers had been heading from the Russian city of Stavropol to Trabzon in Turkey. Initial reports had put the total aboard at about 50.
The plane crashed in a forest near the town of Cherkessk, capital of the ethnic region of Karachayevo-Cherkessiya, at 10.50 a.m. (0750 GMT), the spokesman said.
He gave no reason for the crash.
Russia's air safety standards have plunged since the Soviet state carrier Aeroflot was split into hundreds of smaller domestic companies during market reforms.
The government-owned Rossiiskaya Gazeta daily newspaper said earlier this week that 219 people had been killed last year in 43 air accidents in Russian air space.
